edge_cases: Missing required form fields cause a server error (e.g., KeyError).
Adding a book with a duplicate title triggers a redirect back to the add page.
Login with incorrect username or password returns "Invalid credentials".
Updating or deleting a non‑existent title still returns a success message.
An empty search term returns all books (because the LIKE pattern matches everything).
SQL injection strings are passed directly to queries, potentially altering behavior.
contract.intent: Expose a web API for basic library management: adding books, member login, updating/deleting books, and viewing/searching the catalog.
invariants: Database connections are always closed after each request.
The Books table is queried or modified using the supplied title/author values.
Responses are either plain text strings or HTTP redirects; no JSON is returned.
The Flask app runs with debug mode disabled.
All endpoints use the same MySQL credentials and database (LIBRARYDB).
Title uniqueness is enforced by checking for an existing row before insertion.
io_behavior: POST /add_book with form fields title and author redirects to ./add_book if the title already exists, otherwise redirects to ./view_books.
POST /login_member with form fields username and password returns plain‑text "Login successful" or "Invalid credentials".
POST /update_book_author with form fields title and new_author returns "Author updated successfully".
POST /delete_book with form field title returns "Book deleted successfully".
GET /search_books?term=XYZ returns a string representation of a list of books whose title or author contains the term.
GET /view_books returns a string representation of a list of all books.
side_effects: Inserts a new row into the Books table when a unique title is added.
Updates the Author column of a Books row matching the given title.
Deletes a Books row matching the given title.
Reads from the Members table to verify login credentials.
Each request opens a MySQL connection and closes it before responding.
Redirect responses cause the client to issue a follow‑up request to another endpoint.

rationale: Core endpoints exist but response formats (JSON vs plain text) and redirect targets differ from contract; missing-field handling and duplicate-title redirect violate specified edge cases; many invariants hold (connection closing, debug disabled), side‑effects largely preserved, but overall behavior deviates significantly.
